title: DC-area forecast: Coastal storm to deliver waves of showers Saturday afternoon through Sunday
contentHtml:
Always a human at the helm: Updated around-the-clock by Capital Weather meteorologists.

Happening now: Falling from the 70s into the 60s this evening as breezy conditions persist.

What's next? Highs mid-60s to low 70s Saturday, then a touch cooler Sunday. Winds stay breezy, and a nearby coastal system brings an increasing shower risk from Saturday afternoon through Sunday.

Forecast in detail

Tonight: Mostly to partly clear. Lows range across the 50s. Winds continue from the north near 10 to 15 mph, with gusts around 25 mph. Confidence: Medium-High

Hourly Forecast | Pollen, Air & UV

Tomorrow (Saturday): Some sun during the morning, then clouds increase from east to west through the afternoon. Scattered showers are possible by mid-afternoon, especially near and east of I-95. It stays breezy, with winds from the north and northwest gusting to about 30 mph. Highs range from the mid-60s north and northeast to the low 70s south and southwest. Confidence: Medium

Tomorrow night: Mostly cloudy with scattered showers possible, especially during the evening into early overnight and from near DC or I-95 to the east, although even western areas should see some raindrops. Lows within a few degrees of 55. Confidence: Medium

Sunday: There may be a lull in the morning, but more showers look to rotate in from the north and east during the day. Otherwise, expect mainly cloudy skies and continued gusts to near 30 mph. It won't be the best outdoor day. Highs likely stay in the mid-60s or so, unless skies trend sunnier. Confidence: Low-Medium

A look ahead

Sunday night: Evening showers are possible, then probably tapering off late. Mostly cloudy skies continue, with winds hopefully easing. Lows in the 50s to near 60. Confidence: Low-Medium

More clouds than sun and cooler air may linger into Monday, with highs potentially held within a few degrees of 70. Confidence: Medium

Sunshine and warmth build back in by Tuesday and Wednesday, with highs rising from the mid- to upper 70s Tuesday to the upper 70s to around 80 Wednesday. Confidence: Medium

DC weather history for September 25

Remnants of Hurricane Eloise in 1975 brought a deluge that set a rainfall record, flooded homes and roads, and forced evacuations across the region.

Today’s daily digit — 7/10: Mainly bright but breezy. Still, it’s plenty comfortable with temperatures up a handful of degrees from yesterday. | 🤚 Your call?
The digit is a somewhat subjective rating of the day’s weather, on a 0-to-10 scale.
